newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt impounds Ukraine ferry that hit Red Sea coral.
newsitem.headline: Egypt impounds Ukraine ferry that hit Red Sea coral.

text.p: Egyptian port authorities said on Wednesday they have impounded a Ukrainian ferry that ran aground on a coral reef in the Red Sea last month.

Officials at Sharm el-Sheikh port said prosecutors had ordered the 38-metre (125-foot) Moldova to be impounded as of Friday. The ferry is currently at Suez port until the prosecutors finish their investigation, one official said.
Last month, the ferry struck the Woodhouse reef in the Strait of Tiran while it was sailing to the Black Sea from the Israeli port of Eilat.
The ship was refloated and fixed before being sent to Suez port, the official added.
In April a British cruise liner ran aground in the Strait of Tiran and was detained by the Egyptian government pending payment of $23.5 million in compensation for alleged damage to the coral reef.
Egypt's tourism industry is a vital source of foreign currency and partly relies on Red Sea and Mediterranean diving.
